items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: And in Chicago she used Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band and I was in the band. So that’s how I recorded with her.

ctx.x: And she taught Bessie Smith. She was Bessie Smith’s teacher. And in Chicago she used Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band and I was in the band. So that’s how I recorded with her. She was very nice, a very, very, very nice woman. And we played all of her songs, and that was it. That was about ‘26. And in the 30s, someone gave me an album of it.
What was it like, you know, for our students who are used to hearing what they do to make a record these days you know, in the million dollar studios. What was it like at that time to make a record?

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Yes, she stood in front of the horn, the band was back of her.

ctx.x: And I supposed Ma Rainey stood in front of that horn?
Yes, she stood in front of the horn, the band was back of her.
Uh-huh, and who else was in that band?
